issues.title: Proposal: add crypto-native AML method values (mixer, chain) to the aml registry
issues.author: OceanAlt666
issues.body:
Thanks for the `aml` claim + IANA "AML Methods Values" registry work — the JWT-claim + Expert-Review model is a clean fit for agent payments.

One gap for crypto-native / on-chain agents: the initial values (`ofac`, `sanc`, `watch`, `pep`, `adv`) are shaped for traditional finance and don't cover two checks that a payee-**address** screen routinely performs:

- **`mixer`** — exposure to mixing services / tumblers (e.g. Tornado-type contracts). Distinct from a sanctions-list hit, though the two can co-occur.
- **`chain`** — on-chain risk from tracing: tainted upstream funds (multi-hop), stablecoin issuer freeze (USDT/USDC), and address heuristics. This is the on-chain-native analogue to `adv` (adverse media).

Proposing these two as additional method values (happy to submit via the jwt-reg-review Expert Review process). A payee screen would then emit e.g. `aml: ["ofac", "sanc", "mixer", "chain"]` alongside its result, so a verifier can see *which* methods produced the verdict rather than trusting an opaque pass/fail.

Reference issuer that already produces exactly these categories with verifiable evidence, mapped to a KYA-token `aml` claim: https://github.com/OceanAlt666/agent-compliance-adapters — see `toKyaAmlClaim` in `adapters.mjs`. Glad to draft the registry text if that's useful.
